Each test logs in through the UI (packages/test-helpers/src/login.ts: email OTP read from mailpit, or password) or creates users directly with prisma (tests/test-utils.ts). notes: BUILD-TIME URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is inlined into the build (the build-time value appears in 72 files under apps/web/.next, both server chunks and client static chunks). It drives better-auth baseURL and trustedOrigins (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:59,667-668) and absoluteUrl() links. N instances started from ONE build on different ports will all generate URLs and trust origins for the build-time port, so auth from any other port is expected to fail and redirects/links point at worker 0's app. Either build once per port or give every instance the same origin.
At build time `NODE_ENV=test next build` reads apps/web/.env.test (NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002, PORT=3002) unless the env already sets them; exported env wins.

The Playwright config loads apps/web/.env.test with dotenv (does not override existing env; 15 of 20 keys were injected here). At runtime webServer.env sets __NEXT_PROCESSED_ENV=true, so Next reads no .env file; DATABASE_URL, SMTP_* and SECRET_PASSWORD are read from process env at runtime (not inlined; checked).
CI=true is required: without it the webServer command is `rm -rf .next && next dev`, which deletes the production build and runs a dev server (and reuseExistingServer becomes true).

SHARED MAILPIT: 10 specs call deleteAllMessages() (e.g. authentication.spec.ts:26, otp-sign-up.spec.ts:24, email-invites.spec.ts:97) and captureOne() picks the newest unread mail for a recipient and marks it read. With N workers on one mailpit, one worker wipes or consumes another's OTP mail. Give each worker its own mailpit (distinct --smtp/--listen ports; SMTP_PORT goes to that worker's app, MAILPIT_API_URL to that worker's test process). Both are plain env vars.

Test processes import the prisma client from @rallly/database (tests/test-utils.ts and many specs) and write to the DB directly, using DATABASE_URL from the worker's env. The per-worker DATABASE_URL must be set in the worker before spec files load.
tests/house-keeping.spec.ts calls /api/house-keeping/* with CRON_SECRET: these delete inactive or deleted polls DB-wide. That is safe with one DB per worker but not with a shared one.
Two specs run in serial mode (email-invites.spec.ts:26, list-unsubscribe.spec.ts:22).

BROWSER SHIM: Playwright >= 1.57 expects chrome-linux64/chrome and chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell; revision 1194 ships chrome-linux/{chrome,headless_shell}. Chrome 141 (1194) passed the 1.58.1 suite.
Postgres 16.13 used; CI uses postgres:18-alpine. All migrations applied cleanly on 16.
pnpm 10 skips dependency build scripts (@prisma/engines, esbuild, sharp, ...); CI does the same, and nothing needed them.
Mailpit was built from source with the Go toolchain at /usr/local/go (go install fetched go1.26.8 and modules via proxy.golang.org); GitHub release downloads were not tried.

CONFIG CHOICES: (1) No `build` key: build once outside isolate with the recipe command, because isolate runs build.command on every `run`. (2) db.migrate `pnpm -w run db:deploy`: isolate runs it with cwd apps/web; prisma.config.ts reads DIRECT_DATABASE_URL || DATABASE_URL, hence extraUrlEnvs. No seed: CI does not seed. (3) app.start uses "$PORT": in the dist first read (src/app/apps.ts before 9fe52ac), app.start was spawned raw and only app.env got placeholders. Since 9fe52ac {port} is filled in app.start too, and either form works. `pnpm exec` is needed because isolate spawns `/bin/sh -c` with its own PATH, which lacks node_modules/.bin. (4) app.env repeats 15 .env.test values plus __NEXT_PROCESSED_ENV. playwright.config.ts:4 loads .env.test into the runner's env, and the baseline webServer inherits it. isolate starts apps before that config is loaded, so without these the apps lack CRON_SECRET, SECRET_PASSWORD, WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS, ZOOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN and others that specs rely on (webhooks.spec.ts:22-23, house-keeping.spec.ts:25, zoom-deauthorization.spec.ts:11). (5) healthPath /api/status (src/app/api/status/route.ts).

ARMS (command: `node /home/user/shard/dist/src/cli.js run ... -- pnpm exec playwright test --retries=0`, cwd apps/web). S = the 7-file subset tests/{accessibility,house-keeping,otp-email-locale,otp-sign-up,password-sign-up,stripe-portal-auth,zoom-deauthorization}.spec.ts (21 tests). baseline@1 (`run --baseline -- ... --workers=1 --retries=0`, full): 137 passed, 1 failed, 2 did not run. The failure is email-invites.spec.ts:104, "Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded" at CPU 94% busy, i.e. timeout under load; the 2 skipped tests are its serial siblings. routingValid true, b0 +5121 commits, wall 531 s. isolated@1, full, recipe build: INTERRUPTED by me after 577 s of test phase (projected well over 30 min: 20 of the 24 tests executed failed, most after up to 30 s, and 86 tests were still to come). 54 of 140 tests reached: 3 passed, 20 failed that pass at baseline, 1 interrupted (email-invites:104), 30 serial skips. The isolate reporter wrote nothing (see BUGS), so these counts come from the dot line and test-results/. routingValid true (vacuous, 0 recorded tests), w0 +244. isolated@1 S: 18 passed, 2 failed, 1 did not run. routingValid true, w0 +189. isolated@2 S: 18/2/1, routingValid FALSE (w0 +0, w1 +193). isolated@4 S: 17 passed, 3 failed, 1 did not run. routingValid FALSE (w0 +0, w1 +122, w2 +32, w3 +33). Mitigation isolated@1, full: INTERRUPTED after 578 s. The same 21 failed tests as isolated@1, 3 passed, 30 skipped, w0 +253. Mitigation N=2/N=4: not run, because N=1 showed no improvement.

FAILURES, category BUILD-TIME URL (hazard a), at every N with the recipe build: accessibility.spec.ts:44,:75 (and :81 skipped); admin-setup.spec.ts:36,:54,:69,:83,:97; authentication.spec.ts:30 (plus 15 serial skips); closed-poll-writes.spec.ts:59; comments-disabled.spec.ts:9,:47; conferencing.spec.ts:79; control-panel.spec.ts:30; create-delete-poll.spec.ts:16; cross-timezone.spec.ts:229,:247,:274,:294,:321; edit-options.spec.ts:20. Mechanism: isolate puts app i on http://127.0.0.1:<OS-assigned port> (src/proc/ports.ts listens on port 0), never on the build-time origin, so N=1 is affected as well. `next start` re-reads next.config.ts, so assetPrefix (next.config.ts:32 = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL) follows the runtime app.env value, and the HTML <script> tags point at 127.0.0.1:<port>. The Turbopack client runtime, however, has the build-time chunk base inlined (.next/static/chunks/turbopack-*.js: TURBOPACK_CHUNK_BASE_PATH "http://localhost:3201/_next/"), and so does the RSC payload. Every failed test's trace shows ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED for http://localhost:3201/_next/static/chunks/*.js and /static/logo.svg. The client never hydrates, the login form falls back to a native GET /login?identifier=..., and the steps time out ("waiting for getByRole('heading', { name: /Verify your email|Finish logging in/ })", "waiting for getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Address' })"). Server side, absoluteUrl() is also inlined (packages/utils/src/absolute-url.ts:28), and it drives better-auth baseURL and trustedOrigins (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:59,667-668), so auth would reject the 127.0.0.1 origin even with a hydrated client. Specs that pass under isolation are request-only: house-keeping, zoom-deauthorization, otp-*, password-sign-up, stripe-portal-auth.

FAILURE, category UNMANAGED SERVICE (hazard b), at N=4 only: otp-sign-up.spec.ts:62 "an existing user still signs in with a code" timed out at 30 s on worker 3 (start 5.30 s, 30.0 s long). getCode(existingEmail) at otp-sign-up.spec.ts:75 polls the shared mailpit, and otp-email-locale.spec.ts:25 (beforeEach deleteAllMessages) ran on worker 2 at 5.17 s and 5.51 s, deleting that mail. isolate's two solo reruns passed, so it classified the test flaky. At N=2 both otp specs landed on one worker and it passed. 10 specs call deleteAllMessages(); with a working UI more would collide.

HAZARD (c) VERIFIED (indirectly): specs' Prisma (packages/database/src/client.ts:14 reads DATABASE_URL at import) talks to the worker's database. At N=4, house-keeping.spec.ts on worker 1 inserts polls through Prisma, calls app w1's /api/house-keeping endpoint, and asserts markedDeleted 3 (house-keeping.spec.ts:182). otp-sign-up.spec.ts:40 on worker 3 sets instanceSettings.disableUserRegistration through Prisma (line 16) and gets SIGNUP_DISABLED from app w3 (line 54). Both pass only if the test process and app i share w<i>. dbActivity shows commits on w1..w3. The repo config's dotenv (.env.test DATABASE_URL=...:5450) does not override the env module's value.

ROUTING CHECK FALSE ALARM: at N=2 and N=4, w0 ran only accessibility.spec.ts. With the client broken those tests just view pages and make no database queries (w0's app log shows it served pages, e.g. "Failed to load pay wall pricing"), so w0 has 0 commits and isolate reports "the app probably ignores DATABASE_URL". The app does not ignore it: routing is fine, and the failure is hazard (a).

MITIGATION TRIED (one, no rallly file changed, but a non-recipe build env): build without NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (work/rallly-isolate/build-mitigation.sh): export .env.test values except NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/NODE_ENV, __NEXT_PROCESSED_ENV=true so `NODE_ENV=test next build` does not re-load .env.test, SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 as rallly's own Dockerfile:37 does for runtime-URL builds, and `pnpm turbo build:test --filter=@rallly/web --env-mode=loose`. The runtime URL then comes from app.env NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL={url}. Result: the build has no localhost:3201/3002 anywhere and TURBOPACK_CHUNK_BASE_PATH is "/_next/". No request is refused any more, but the client still never hydrates: the same 21 tests fail at N=1, and the login form submits as a native GET. Probes outside isolate (work/rallly-isolate/probe-server.sh + probe-hydration.cjs, checking React props on the "Continue with email" button): recipe build on its build-time origin localhost:3201 hydrates (control). Mitigation build with runtime NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3202 does not hydrate: assetPrefix, re-read at runtime, is absolute while the build's chunk base is "/_next/", with no console or page errors. Mitigation build with NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL unset at runtime does hydrate, but it needs SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION (env.ts:207 requires the URL) and the page then says "Login is currently not configured.". Upstream's Docker image avoids this because standalone output freezes next.config at build time. Conclusion: with `next start`, rallly's assetPrefix = NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL coupling makes a per-worker runtime URL impossible from one build. The brief's other idea, building with the URL of a worker's port, is impossible because isolate chooses ports at random.

WHAT WOULD COUNT AS "WITH MODIFICATIONS" (not done): editing apps/web/next.config.ts so assetPrefix does not follow NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, then using the runtime-URL build. Untested hypothesis: this plus app.env NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL={url} would hydrate and match better-auth trustedOrigins per worker.

BLOCKER and PROPOSALS for hazard (a): (P1, preferred) an isolate "shared origin" mode, the D-001 option (c). isolate runs one reverse proxy on the build-time origin (here localhost:3201) that routes each request to app i by the x-isolate-worker header, which `run --tag-requests` already adds through extraHTTPHeaders and so on every browser request, subresources included. The wrapper then sets baseURL to that origin for every worker, and app.env NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the same origin, so runtime assetPrefix = build chunk base = better-auth trusted origin. One build is enough, and links in mails, which point at the build-time origin, route correctly when opened in the worker's page. (P2) pinned per-worker ports (e.g. app.basePort, port = base + i) plus a per-worker build step with {i}/{port}/{url} in build.command and per-worker output dirs: N builds of 2.5-4 min each. (P3) a rallly change (see WITH MODIFICATIONS).

PROPOSAL for hazard (b), not tested: config alone can give each worker its own mailpit, e.g. app.env SMTP_PORT "331{i}" plus playwright.env MAILPIT_API_URL "http://127.0.0.1:332{i}/api", with N mailpits started by hand. But isolate reruns start apps with index N+run (src/report/rerun.ts: index = databases.length + run; the logs show "app w4 ... database rerun0"), so a rerun app would point at a mailpit that does not exist. Fix: reruns reuse the failed test's worker index for {i}, or isolate manages per-worker sidecars (a `services` list with a start command, per-worker ports and env).

ISOLATE BUGS / GAPS (src not edited): (1) routing check false positive: "no committed transactions on w0 ... the app probably ignores DATABASE_URL" when a worker's tests simply made no DB queries. PLAN §5.5 also calls for per-app request counts; fix: count HTTP requests per app (a counting proxy, or a request hook in the app preload) and report "served N requests, 0 DB commits" instead of blaming DATABASE_URL. (2) After an interrupt (SIGINT to isolate) the isolate reporter writes nothing ("Playwright exited without writing the isolate reporter results"), and the report then says routing: valid with 0 tests. Fix: append each test result to the results file in onTestEnd, and report routing as "unknown" when there are no results. (3) Reruns reuse the repo's outputDir, and Playwright empties it at the start of each invocation, so after reruns test-results/ holds only the last rerun's artifacts: the main run's traces are lost (seen in all three subset arms). Fix: pass `--output .isolate/reruns/<n>` to rerun invocations. (4) Rerun apps get {i}/ISOLATE_WORKER_INDEX = N+run (see hazard b). (5) `init` was advertised in the CLI usage before commands/init.js existed (raw "Cannot find module" error); fixed by the F2 integration. (6) init health-path detection misses /api/status; init's db.seed guess adds data that CI does not have. (7) The config's unmanaged.services list is ignored by run: the report lists the scanner's six services, not the one actually used (mailpit). (8) Minor: isolate adds its generated files to .git/info/exclude but not .isolate/, which shows up as untracked in the rallly checkout.

definitions.testPhaseMs: first test begin to last test end, from the isolate reporter (the verdict span)
definitions.wallMs: the isolate command's whole wall time from its report (setup, build, Postgres, migrate/seed, clone, app boot, tests, reruns, teardown)
definitions.preTestMs: Playwright start to first test begin: webServer boot, globalSetup, worker and browser start
definitions.playwrightWallMs: pre-test + test phase + post-test: Playwright alone
definitions.endToEndMs: wallMs minus the build phase (done once before timing) and the failure reruns
definitions.valid: a run counts when it wrote a report and results, stayed under the 45-min cap, routing was valid, no "too many clients", and its per-test outcomes equal baseline@1's reference outcomes (most frequent outcome over its timed rounds)
definitions.speedups: medians of valid timed runs: test phase, Playwright wall ("wall") and end-to-end of isolated@1 divided by those of isolated@N; vs-baseline divides the baseline arm by isolated@N
definitions.harnessEffect: test phase of baseline@1 / isolated@1; outside 0.85-1.15 it is flagged and vs-baseline speedups should not be quoted
definitions.schedulingCeiling: T1 / max(T1/N, longest file); T1 = sum of per-test median durations at isolated@1; a file is its longest test if two of its tests were seen running at once in an isolated N > 1 run, else the sum of its tests
definitions.resourceCeiling: min(N, cores/d); d = machine-wide busy CPU seconds (busyPct x cores x Playwright wall) per test-phase second at isolated@1 (includes Postgres, the app and anything else on the machine)
definitions.perTestInflation: sum of test durations at N / at N=1 (medians over valid runs)
definitions.setupFraction: sum of hook and fixture time / sum of test durations; pre-test and post-test shares of the Playwright wall
definitions.isolationFailure: fails in >= 2 isolated@4 timed rounds and passes in >= 2 baseline@1 timed rounds
definitions.memory: peak RSS of every app tree plus the Postgres tree at the largest N that ran (each tree sampled once a second, peaks summed)
definitions.cacheEffect: the cold run (fresh .isolate/, before everything) against the valid timed isolated@1 runs; never part of a speedup
